_readme: The evaluation contract for this project. Every claim the README makes about
GraphRAG versus RAG is measured against this file by `python run.py eval`.
category            what kind of retrieval problem this is
expected_advantage  which strategy family SHOULD win, decided before any
measurement was taken. Questions where GraphRAG is
expected to lose or draw are included deliberately -
a benchmark that only contains questions your system
required_documents  document ids that must appear in retrieved context for
the retrieval to be considered complete
required_terms      strings that must appear in a correct answer. Matched
forbidden_terms     strings whose presence indicates a specific known
needs_graph_fact    true when the answer cannot be quoted from any document
and must come from a traversal

questions.question: Typhoon Meilin has shut down Kaohsiung for about three weeks. Which of our finished products are exposed, and through which suppliers?
questions.notes: The flagship question. No document states which products are exposed - the incident bulletin explicitly says so. The answer is a join across Location, Site, Supplier, DEPENDS_ON, Component and Product. All four products are exposed: NW-500 through Kaigan directly and through Formosa-to-Meridian, NW-220 and TX-9 and AQ-100 through the Formosa-to-Meridian board path, TX-9 and AQ-100 also through Sentinel directly.

questions.question: Is our dual sourcing on the LI-18650 battery pack genuine, or do the two suppliers share an upstream dependency?
questions.notes: Which suppliers supply this component is an ERP fact. What each buys upstream is in two different documents. The intersection appears nowhere. The 2026 risk review states that this question cannot be answered from any single record, which is the point.

questions.question: What did the 2026 Prahara Polymers audit say about the fire suppression system?
questions.notes: Included so the project can demonstrate where GraphRAG is NOT worth it. The answer sits in one section of one document. Vector search finds it in one call; the graph strategies spend extra queries and latency to arrive at the same place.

questions.question: Under our dual sourcing policy, what makes a component require a second source?
questions.notes: A policy lookup. There is no relationship to traverse and no advantage to be had. A GraphRAG system that cannot answer this as well as plain RAG has regressed.

questions.question: Which engineering change notice covers the PCB-A7 revision C change, and does it alter the laminate specification?
questions.notes: Part numbers and document numbers are exactly what dense embeddings are worst at and BM25 is best at. Included to justify why the honest baseline in this project is vector+BM25 rather than vector alone.

questions.question: Which finished products depend on NdFeB rare earth magnets, and what regulatory exposure does that create?
questions.notes: Magnets reach us through Helios only, so only the NW-220 is affected. The forbidden terms are the interesting part: a system that pattern-matches 'which products' and lists all four is wrong, and this question catches it.

questions.question: Which sole-sourced components come from a supplier that currently has an open audit finding?
questions.notes: Joins a structured attribute (sole_source, from the ERP) against an extracted one (an open finding, from an audit PDF). Neither source can answer it alone, which is the practical argument for one graph over a warehouse plus a vector store.

questions.question: Who manufactures the TFT panel inside the DSP-3300 display module?
questions.notes: The corpus explicitly records that Kaigan declines to name this supplier. The correct answer is to say so and cite the transparency register - not to guess a plausible panel maker. Any named panel manufacturer here is a hallucination.

questions.question: What was Meridian Circuits annual revenue in 2025?
questions.notes: Nothing in the corpus contains this. Unlike GQ-08 there is not even a record of the gap. The system must say it does not know. A model that answers from general knowledge fails, and richer retrieval does not help - which is worth showing, because it means retrieval quality and refusal quality are separate problems.

questions.question: If Sarawak Copper Foil stopped shipping, which Northwind products would eventually be affected and how many tiers away is that supplier?
questions.notes: The deepest question in the set. Sarawak is tier 3 and appears in exactly one document, which names only its immediate customer. Getting from there to a finished product is three further hops through data that lives in two other documents and a CSV.

questions.question: Which of our products fall under the EU Battery Regulation due diligence obligations?
questions.notes: The regulation names the component. Which products contain that component is a bill-of-materials fact in the CSV. The AQ-100 has no battery, so listing it is a specific, checkable error - and it is exactly the error a system that reasons from the regulation document alone will make.

questions.question: Sentinel Optics has an open ESD finding. Which products does that put at risk, and do we have a second source for the affected parts?
questions.notes: Needs both halves. The finding and its ESD detail are in a document that vector search finds easily. Which parts Sentinel supplies, which products those sit in, and whether a second source exists are all structural. Expected to be the clearest hybrid win in the set.
